title: Rapid Hire Surge — 72hr Onboard Capsule & Interview Rubric
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight operational playbook for rapid hiring bursts (small-mid scale: 5–20 hires) where time-to-offer and rapid, consistent onboarding matter. The goal is to reduce recruiter+hiring-manager back-and-forth, keep candidate experience cohesive, and ensure new joiners are productive within 72 hours of start for essential tasks.

Scope and when to use this capsule:
- Use when headcount needs to be filled in a short window (e.g., product launch, contractual runway, seasonal hiring).
- Not intended for senior IC or manager roles unless explicitly approved by people-ops/comp.
- Pairs with existing onboarding pipelines but prioritizes a compressed first-3-day onboarding schedule.

Quick checklist: pre-acceptance (recruiter):
- Confirm offer sign-off and comp stamping (recruiter -> hiring manager -> finance).
- Share 72h preboard packet URL w/ candidate immediately after verbal offer: packet includes day0 checklist, required account forms, laptop options, and buddy intro.
- Open access request ticket in IT queue with candidate name and tentative start date (use rapid-hire template).
- Send manager a one-page role activation brief (2 bullets: day1 deliverable, 30-day deliverable).

Interview rubric (single-sheet, consistent scoring):
Scoring scale: 1 = strong no; 2 = below bar; 3 = meets bar; 4 = strong yes; 5 = exceptional.
Required rubric sections (all roles):
- Core competency (role specific): evidence of required skill (coding, infra, customer success playbook).
- Problem decomposition & reasoning: how the candidate structures unknowns and tradeoffs.
- Ownership & follow-through: examples of end-to-end ownership, shipping, incident handling.
- Communication & collaboration: clarity, ability to adapt audience, feedback orientation.
- Culture and grit: alignment with Redwood values (product-focused engineering, operational rigor, customer empathy).
Guidance:
- Minimum passing threshold: average >= 3 across all sections AND no section scored <= 2 unless hiring manager signs off.
- Strong hire signal: average >= 4 and at least two 5s.
- Reject flag: any behavioural safety concern or factual mismatch on critical requirements.

Behavioral prompts and probes (short):
- Ownership probe: "Describe a time you discovered a production problem outside your code ownership. What did you do?"
- Tradeoff probe: "You have two weeks to deliver a feature with flaky infra; what do you prioritize and why?"
- Collaboration probe: "Tell me about a time you changed your approach after teammate feedback — what changed and why?"

Interview logistics for surge windows:
- Panel composition: 1 cross-functional interviewer (buddy pool), 1 hiring manager, 1 technical peer. Keep panels to 45 minutes max (30–35 practical + 10 wrap).
- Interviewer prep: use the 5-min prebrief doc: main outcome, 2 mandatory probes, 1 no-go question. Share at least 24 hours before interview.
- Timeboxing: use structured timeline: 5 min intro, 20–25 min core probe/problem, 10 min deep-dive behavioral, 5 min candidate Q&A.

Rapid decision workflow (24–48h target):
- After interview, interviewers submit rubric within 3 hours. Recruiter aggregates and triggers an async debrief thread in hiring channel.
- Hiring manager makes decision within 24 hours of final interview. If consensus is mixed, escalate to people-ops for calibration with one additional interviewer.

Offer & preboarding templates (copyable):
- Candidate message (verbal offer follow-up): short, personal, 3 bullets: comp, start date window, link to preboard packet.
- Manager welcome template: short orientation note to candidate, buddy intro, top-3 first-week priorities.

72-hour onboarding capsule (day0 to day3):
Preboarding (day -7 to 0):
- Candidate completes new-hire forms, picks laptop, submits ID for badge.
- IT greenlights accounts (email, Slack, GitHub, Jira) and self-serve drives access.
- Buddy assigned and intro message scheduled to post on day0 morning.

Day0 (start-of-day, before first meeting):
- Manager: short 30-min welcome call (expectations + top 3 outcomes).
- Admin: hardware handoff, base access validated, account walk-through.
- Buddy: 60-min walkthrough of local dev setup, critical repos, and core runbooks.
- Quick wins: assign a 2-hour low-risk task that touches production minimally (example: update a minor doc + submit PR) so the new hire ships something before EOD.

Day1: role immersion & context
- Morning: product/team orientation (30–45 min) + roadmap overview.
- Afternoon: pair session with peer on a small integration or test harness; shadow on-call rotation basics (if applicable).
- End-of-day: 30-min sync with manager to set 7-day goals.

Day2-3: ramp and remove friction
- Deep-dive on systems and infra diagrams; practical troubleshooting session with SRE or infra buddy.
- Access escalation review: ensure all tickets resolved or queued w/ ETA.
- First 72h retrospective (manager + buddy + new hire): capture blockers and update onboarding playbook.

30-day baseline expectations (short):
- New hire completes checklist of 8 core tasks (accesses, one shipped PR, test coverage, one stakeholder 1:1).
- Manager sets a 30-day impact metric (quantitative where possible).

Interviewer calibration & notes for surge:
- Run a 30-min calibration drop-in before first surge round: review rubric anchors with 3 sample past hires (anonymized).
- Share examples of 2/3 borderline notes to align thresholds.
- Encourage fast scoring; avoid long subjective paragraphs — bullet evidence only.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: rushed decisions degrade quality. Mitigation: require at least one senior interviewer sign-off for every hire when time-to-hire < 72 hours.
- Risk: access delays. Mitigation: pre-open generic role accounts and convert to personal accounts on start date.

Metrics to track (post-surge retro):
- Time-to-offer, time-to-start, percent of hires meeting 72h active target, 30-day retention, manager satisfaction score (1–5).

Appendix: quick templates and links (copyable)
- Manager activation brief (one-liner): Role name + 3 bullet outcomes + 30-day metric.
- Candidate preboard packet link (placeholder): https://drive.redwood/rapid-onboard-packet
- IT ticket template subject: "Rapid Hire — {{candidate}} — Start {{date}}"

Notes and open questions:
- Consider adding a small stipend for expedited shipping of hardware in global regions — cross-check with finance.
- Evaluate whether 72h model scales above 20 hires without adding a dedicated ops coordinator.
- Review legal requirements for specific countries re: hiring lead time and documentation.

Document history and authorship note:
- Drafted by Sofia Martinez (people-ops) with input from Eng managers (Daniel Park) and IT ops (Lena Novak).
- Use, iterate, and file feedback to Confluence page linked in artifacts.
